pins.name: GPIO0
pins.label: GPIO0 (Led active low)
pins.notes:
Must be HIGH or floating for normal boot; LOW at boot enters flash/programming mode. No interrupt support. No onboard user button on this board (checked - see notes.txt) - only non-GPIO RST/EN control pins are present. Onboard red LED (active-low, LED_BUILTIN) - confirmed via Adafruit Learning Guide, see chipGpios note
Onboard red LED (active-low) — see pfodWeb NOTE above pinNotes for sources

pins.name: GPIO1
pins.label: GPIO1
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 TX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: GPIO2
pins.label: GPIO2
pins.notes: Must be HIGH at boot. Commonly wired to the on-board LED on dev boards

pins.name: GPIO3
pins.label: GPIO3
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 RX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: SS
pins.label: SS (GPIO15)
pins.notes: Must be LOW at boot (tied to GND via resistor on most boards)

pins.name: GPIO16
pins.label: GPIO16
pins.notes: RTC-domain pin: no internal pull-up/down, no PWM, no interrupt support. Commonly wired to RST for deep-sleep wake

pins.name: A0
pins.label: A0 (GPIO17)
pins.notes: Analog input only (A0) — cannot be used for digital I/O or PWM. Native range is 0-1.0V on the bare chip; Adafruit's own guide documents A0 on this board as ~1.0V max with no on-board divider extending the range - see adc note below
